author: Mark Atwood
text:
DESIGN: GCP-6.5 slot-claim COSE_Sign1 — canonical signing input, wire budget, replay gate, cross-impl impact.

Context: current code signs/verifies only "SLOT_CLAIM:%02X:%IID:%08X" (ordinal/IID/superframe_id) at coap_slot_coord.c:316-337, so the slots array is forgeable (attach captured sig to attacker slots; lowest-IID resolution at :354 then favors the forgery). decode_claim (:800-856) parses a string-key map with no signature/expiry/claim_seq; struct has has_signature (coap_slot_coord.h:121) but zero setters (sibling bead project-LICHEN-worker6-mx8y) and no expiry/claim_seq fields (:112-122). POST handler discards everything at LICHEN_CLAIM_REJECT_NO_SIG -> return 0 (:1020-1024).

=== D1. Envelope (decided within GCP-6.5 mandate; no human policy bead needed) ===
COSE_Sign1 per spec/08:121-199 (RFC 9052): [ protected bstr, unprotected {4: kid=IID}, payload bstr, 48-byte sig bstr ]. Protected = canonical {1: -65537} (Schnorr48-Ed25519). Signing input = SHA256(CBOR(Sig_structure)) per spec/08:177, Sig_structure = ["Signature1", protected, h'', payload]. This SHA-256 prehash is the established house convention: python/src/lichen/crypto/capability_announcements.py:_build_sig_structure (8.12) and test/vectors/generate_gcp_handoff_cose_sign1.py:67 with vectors gcp_handoff_cose_sign1.json. schnorr48.sign/verify take arbitrary-length msg and hash internally (draft-lichen-schnorr-00 4.2; python/src/lichen/crypto/schnorr48.py:109,141). Envelope-vs-raw-signature-over-canonical-CBOR: spec already answers (COSE_Sign1); sibling bead mx8y's "extend the claim format to carry the GCP-6.5 envelope" is satisfied by this design; has_signature bool + raw signature[] field become structurally redundant (4th array element) and should be removed, not given setters.

=== D2. Canonical signing input (payload map) ===
Signature covers canonical CBOR (RFC 8949 4.2.1 core deterministic) of the payload map. Integer keys sort by encoded-byte length then bytewise; keys 1..7 are all single-byte, so canonical field order = numeric order:
  1: slots            array[uint]  sorted ascending, unique (Python invariant slot_claim.py:110-115)
  2: superframe_epoch uint32
  3: mode             0=interleaved, 1=contiguous (spec/08:148)
  4: expiry           uint32 unix seconds UTC
  5: gateway_iid      bstr(8)
  6: claim_seq        uint32
  7: ordinal          uint  [ADDED to spec payload table]
Rationale for key 7: process_claim feeds claim->ordinal into lichen_slot_coord_register_gateway receiver-side (coap_slot_coord.c:376) and the task field list includes ordinal. gateway_count (h:117) and slot_start (h:119) are sender-side selection metadata with no receiver consumer -> NOT carried. cbor2.dumps(canonical=True) (slot_claim.py:214) already produces this encoding.
SPEC BUG FOUND (fix in spec child): spec/08:135 protected example h'a10139ffff' decodes to {1: -65536}, not -65537. Correct bytes: h'47A1013A00010000' (bstr-wrapped a1 01 3a 00010000; verified with cbor2). Text {1: -65537} at :135 and alg ID everywhere else are correct; only the hex is wrong. Also: :195 says 2.04 Changed but impl returns 2.01 (:1043); :196 says 4.09 with winning claim but impl sends NULL payload (:1020) — align in C child.

=== D3. Wire placement + byte budgets (255-byte LoRa PHY payload, spec/02a:21) ===
expiry (key 4) and claim_seq (key 6) live INSIDE the signed payload map — the signature covers them; an attacker cannot strip/re-write without invalidating. Budgets (canonical CBOR, uint32 fields):
  element                          typical (N=4)   worst (N=60, 2-byte slots)
  COSE array hdr                        1               1
  protected bstr (8B: 47 a1013a00010000) 8               8
  unprotected bstr (12B: a1 04 48 +IID) 12              12
  payload map                           43             156
    - map hdr 1; slots 1+1+2N; epoch 6; mode 2; expiry 6; iid 10; seq 6; ordinal 2
  signature bstr (1+48)                49              49
  COSE_Sign1 total                    114             227
For comparison, today's unsigned string-key claim is ~76 B (N=4) and carries no sig/expiry/seq at all. CoAP (~6) + OSCORE option (~10-14) + SCHC-compressed IPv6/UDP (~10-18, spec/03) add ~25-45 B on-air: typical N<=4 claim ~150-160 B fits 255 comfortably; worst-case 60-slot claim (227+30) does NOT. Recommendation for spec child: on-LoRa claims SHOULD cap at ~40 slots (envelope ~195 B); larger allocations use backbone transport. uint64 expiry/seq would add 3 B each — unnecessary (uint32 expiry good to 2106; 2^32 claims).

=== D4. Replay gate ===
Receiver-side per-gateway claim_seq high-water, NV-persisted. Spec/08:193,220 mandates reject-if-<= and :212-214 mandates persistence, but only defines the SENDER side of persistence; the receiver cache spec gap is closed by the spec child (MUST persist receiver cache too).
Storage: Zephyr settings subsystem, root "lichen/slot_claim", one entry per gateway IID (16 hex chars -> uint32). Template: lichen/subsys/lichen/link/replay_settings.c:1-76 — SETTINGS_STATIC_HANDLER_DEFINE(lichen_slot_claim, ...), dual-blob A/B wear-leveling pattern, K_MUTEX. RAM cache: CONFIG_LICHEN_SLOT_COORD_MAX_GATEWAYS entries {iid[8], seq u32, valid}; lazy settings_load_subtree at first use; loaded at coord init.
Gate order inside process_claim (coap_slot_coord.c:299-341):
  1. structural sig presence (replaces has_signature check at :300)
  2. key-store lookup (:310) + schnorr48_verify over SHA256(CBOR(Sig_structure)) — replaces :316-337 string reconstruction
  3. expiry > now (spec step 7, :192) -> else 4.03
  4. claim_seq > cached[IID] (spec step 8, :193); on accept, PERSIST new high-water BEFORE conflict resolution (:341-365) — persist-first is safe: a burned seq only forces the legitimate sender to increment (spec :219); the reverse ordering reopens the replay window if the node crashes between apply and persist
  5. conflict resolution (lowest IID)
New enum value LICHEN_CLAIM_REJECT_REPLAY = 5 (coap_slot_coord.h:83-93) -> 4.03 Forbidden (validation failure per :198; sig failures stay silent-discard per :199). Cache eviction follows gateway-table eviction; pruning is out of scope here.

=== D5. Response codes (aligned while touching, per parent bead) ===
accepted -> 2.04 Changed (spec :195; impl :1043 wrongly 2.01); conflict -> 4.09 with winning gateway's claim as payload (spec :196; impl :1020 sends NULL); missing/invalid sig -> silent discard, return 0 (:1020-1024) but log at WARN with rate limiting (mx8y ask; LOG_DBG at :301 is compiled out at default level); expired/replay/invalid slots -> 4.03.

=== D6. Cross-impl impact ===
- Python (gateway oracle): python/src/lichen/gateway/slot_claim.py is the OLD model — string-keyed to_cbor_map (:129-142), signature over raw canonical claim map (:196-253), no COSE, no expiry/claim_seq (only optional timestamp :94). Epic project-LICHEN-worker6-qpco (qpco.1/.6/.7/.9) owns the Python migration; hand it D2 (7-key map, key 7 ordinal) and D1 (SHA256(CBOR(Sig_structure)) already its convention).
- Rust: rust/lichen-gateway/src/slot.rs has a divergent transcript model (verify_gateway_message at :532, verify_slot_replay_seal at :794-800). qpco.2 owns migration: transcript signing MUST be retired for /slots claims in favor of COSE_Sign1 (transcript machinery may remain for other messages). Its existing replay-seal concept maps onto D4's high-water.
- Vectors: existing test/vectors/gcp_slot_claim.json + gcp6_slot_coordination.json encode the old model; keep until cross-validation, then retire. New gcp_slot_claim_cose_sign1.json + generator modeled on generate_gcp_handoff_cose_sign1.py.

=== Decomposition (5 children, each with acceptance criteria) ===
1. [task] Spec: GCP-6.5 text fixes + payload key 7 + receiver-cache normative text
2. [task] Zephyr C: COSE_Sign1 decode + verify + gating + response codes in coap_slot_coord.c (supersedes the mx8y decode gap; lands with it)
3. [task] Zephyr C: receiver-side NV claim_seq persistence + replay gate
4. [task] Vectors: gcp_slot_claim_cose_sign1.json + generator (replay/expiry/mutation cases; cross-ref qpco.4/qpco.8)
5. [task] Cross-validation review: Python/Rust/Zephyr parity against vectors; confirm Rust transcript retirement; confirm mx8y WARN logging (cross-ref qpco.5)
Dependencies: 2<-1, 3<-2, 4<-1, 5<-2,3,4 and coordinated with qpco epic children.
